answer:
Perform a variable-cell relaxation (vc-relax) of BiFeO3 in the R3c rhombohedral space group with 10 atoms per primitive cell (2 Fe, 2 Bi, 6 O), followed by a self-consistent field (SCF) calculation on the relaxed structure.
Use PseudoDojo SR_v0.4.1 LDA pseudopotentials located at PseudoDojo/SR_v0.4.1/LDA_standard/bi.upf, PseudoDojo/SR_v0.4.1/LDA_standard/fe.upf, and PseudoDojo/SR_v0.4.1/LDA_standard/o.upf.
Build a starting structure from the well-known R3c perovskite BiFeO3 lattice: rhombohedral cell with a = b = c = 5.576 Angstrom, alpha = beta = gamma = 59.7 degrees, and standard internal atomic positions for Bi at (0, 0, 0) + R, Fe at (0.235, 0.235, 0.235) + R, O at (0.537, 0.015, 0.498) + R with appropriate symmetry-equivalent sites to fill 10 atoms.
Set spin-polarized calculation (ISPIN=2) with G-type antiferromagnetic ordering: starting_magnetization(+0.6) on one Fe site and starting_magnetization(-0.6) on the other Fe site, Bi and O at 0.0, since G-type AFM is the experimentally established ground state of BiFeO3 and ISPIN=1 would yield an incorrect metallic solution for an Fe oxide under LDA.
Set occupations = fixed (no smearing) because BiFeO3 is an insulator in its G-type AFM ground state.
Set ecutwfc = 60 Ry and ecutrho = 480 Ry (8x ecutwfc ratio for ultrasoft-like convergence safety with LDA pseudopotentials).
Set k-points as a Monkhorst-Pack grid of 4 x 4 x 4 with a half-grid shift (offset = 0.5, 0.5, 0.5) for the rhombohedral cell.
For the vc-relax: set etot_conv_thr = 1.0e-8, forc_conv_thr = 1.0e-7, press_conv_thr to 0.5 kbar (reasonable default), cell_dofree = all, and allow both ions and cell shape/volume to relax.
For the subsequent SCF: use the relaxed structure (cell parameters and atomic positions from vc-relax output), set conv_thr = 1.0e-8, keep ecutwfc, ecutrho, k-points, occupations, ISPIN, and starting_magnetization identical to the vc-relax run, and set calculation = scf with no ionic or cell relaxation.
Output the fully relaxed structure (cell vectors and fractional atomic coordinates) and the final SCF total energy in Hartree.
